title: Dhanush Says No Diwali or Pongal Feels Complete Without Solomon Pappaiah
excerpt: The Tamil actor marked Diwali with a post on X remembering the late Pattimandram moderator, writing that he cannot remember a Diwali or Pongal without him since childhood.
body:
• Tamil actor Dhanush marked Diwali on Sunday with a post on X remembering Solomon Pappaiah, the Tamil scholar and Pattimandram debate moderator who died about two months ago at the age of 90.
  • "I cannot remember a Diwali or Pongal without him since childhood," Dhanush wrote of Pappaiah, whose televised Tamil debates were a festival fixture in Tamil households.
  • Pappaiah, a Tamil professor at The American College in Madurai for more than three decades, received the Kalaimamani in 2000 and the Padma Shri in 2021, according to PTI reporting.
  • Dhanush had posted about watching Pappaiah's Pattimandram on Diwali as far back as 2016, writing that certain things never change.

For many Tamil households, Diwali and Pongal television meant one voice. On Sunday, actor Dhanush — who works primarily in Tamil cinema — shared on X that a festival is not complete for him without reminiscing about Solomon Pappaiah, the scholar and debate moderator who died around two months ago, most popular for his moderation of Pattimandram, the traditional Tamil debate format, on national television, according to Cinema Express.

"Professor Solomon Pappaiah, who revered Tamil. I cannot remember a Diwali or Pongal without him since childhood."

— Dhanush, in a post on X reported by Cinema Express

Who Solomon Pappaiah was

Pappaiah was a renowned Tamil scholar and television personality who popularised Pattimandram, taking discussions beyond classical literature to contemporary social issues and everyday subjects, according to PTI reporting carried by Andhra Vilas. He served as a Tamil professor at The American College in Madurai for more than three decades. He died in Madurai at the age of 90; PTI reported he died following an illness. His contribution to Tamil literature and public discourse was recognised with the Kalaimamani award in 2000 and the Padma Shri in 2021. Vijay, Rajinikanth and Vijay Sethupathi were among those who paid tribute when he died, Sethupathi writing that he had taken Pattimandram from home to home, speaking Tamil simply and beautifully.

A connection that predates this Diwali

This is not the first time Dhanush has reminisced about the scholar on social media. Cinema Express reports that in 2016, the actor said he watched Pattimandram with Solomon on Diwali, writing, "Yet another festival with Solomon Pappaiah Pattimandram. Certain things never change," while mentioning childhood memories. Dhanush has not starred in a film with Solomon, but his posts indicate a deep connection with the scholar and orator. In Sunday's post, going off on a tangent, Dhanush said he found Raja, who participated in a Pattimandram that Pappaiah mediated, an appropriate choice for his role in Sivaji. He signed off: "Pappaiya sir, your voice and memories will live in our hearts forever."

The scholar who mostly stayed out of cinema

Tamil cinema audiences knew Pappaiah through cameo appearances in films including Mudhalvan, Boys and Shankar's Sivaji: The Boss with Rajinikanth. Cinema Express reports that he had reportedly rejected more than 200 film roles, and once told The Hindu that he did not accept numerous film offers because he did not feel he belonged in that sphere. It also reports that he expressed regret for being part of Sivaji over a scene involving body shaming and colourism towards his onscreen daughters, publicly apologised multiple times on television for taking part in it, and that this played a part in him quitting acting altogether.

Why the post resonates beyond Tamil Nadu

Pattimandram debates were festival-day viewing for Tamil families, in India and across the diaspora, which is why a moderator's absence registers two festivals running. Dhanush's post, made on Diwali itself, frames that absence plainly: the programmes that structured festival mornings since his childhood are now a memory of the man who led them. For Tamil readers abroad who grew up with the same broadcasts at family gatherings, the tribute names a shared experience rather than a celebrity connection — Pappaiah never acted alongside Dhanush, and the bond the actor describes is a viewer's, formed from childhood festival viewing.
